why: Reach the 55-source floor: remittance rules (US State Dept 2026), a bubble-tea listing count (Uber Eats, 3 Nov), and the census Muslim share (KNBS 2019), with every line that said otherwise brought into line.

edits.value: Chicken, coffee and forecourt food are growing. Burger, kebab and plant-based have no current count.

edits.find: We made no locator counts for this issue: every count is a company report or press, and the row says which.
edits.replace: We made one listing count (bubble tea, on Uber Eats); every other count is a company report or press, and the row says which.

edits.value: No international entrant found. Uber Eats’ Nairobi bubble-tea page listed nine boba outlets under six names on 3 Nov 2026, a listing rather than a full count. Panda Tea had four, selling milk tea beside Korean fried chicken; the rest had one each. Nearest proxy for demand: Ketepa opened a Nairobi tea house in 2018 and said Kenyans drink 37m kg of tea, under 10% of what the country grows.
A tea-drinking country where bubble tea is still small and local.

Ketepa’s 2018 Nairobi tea house, and 37m kg of local tea consumption. The largest boba seller on Uber Eats lists four Nairobi outlets; no international entrant found. Demand data: Not found. [S30, S54]

edits.find: Muslims are about 11% of the population (2021).
edits.replace: Muslims were 10.9% of Kenyans at the 2019 census, and 38% in Mombasa.

edits.find: Remittance rules: not found from a primary source.
edits.replace: No restrictions on converting or transferring investment funds; profits may be repatriated after tax.
